target.summary: Determine why a synthetic checkout contract test produces an order-dependent total.

blocker.observed_failure: The synthetic total differs when the same discount identifiers are supplied in a different order.
blocker.expected_behavior: The synthetic total remains stable for equivalent discount sets regardless of input order.

steps: Run the synthetic contract fixture with discount identifiers in ascending order.
Run the same fixture with the identical identifiers in reverse order.

observations.statement: The failure reproduces when the synthetic identifiers are reversed while the data values remain unchanged.
A slower synthetic run also failed, so elapsed time initially correlated with the symptom.
Canonicalizing identifier order removes the failure while all synthetic values remain constant.

hypotheses.statement: The synthetic aggregation path is order-sensitive because identifiers are consumed without canonical ordering.
Execution timing causes the synthetic total mismatch.

verification_tests.procedure: Hold the synthetic values constant and canonicalize only identifier ordering before aggregation.
verification_tests.expected_disconfirming_signal: The total mismatch persists after canonical ordering is applied.

verification_tests.procedure: Hold identifier ordering constant while varying the synthetic execution delay.
verification_tests.expected_disconfirming_signal: The failure follows delay changes even when ordering is fixed.

root_cause.rationale: The failure follows input ordering and disappears under a controlled ordering-only change; the timing alternative was independently falsified.

minimum_next_step.action: Apply a bounded synthetic fix that canonicalizes identifier order before aggregation without changing calculation semantics.
minimum_next_step.validation: Run the existing synthetic contract fixture in both identifier orders plus the ordering-isolation regression.
minimum_next_step.expected_signal: Both orderings produce the same expected synthetic total and the regression remains green.
minimum_next_step.stop_condition: Stop and request owner review if the repair requires broader contract or business-semantic changes.

proposed_fix_scope: canonicalize synthetic identifier ordering before aggregation
fix_readiness.rationale: The failure is reproducible, the ordering hypothesis has controlled verification evidence, and the material timing alternative is falsified.

inference_summary: The ordering hypothesis is the bounded causal explanation supported by the current synthetic evidence.
uncertainty: No production behavior or real downstream system was evaluated.

unknowns.statement: Whether any private downstream implementation has the same ordering behavior is unknown.

assumptions: The synthetic contract fixture represents only the public conformance scenario described here.

human_confirmation_points: A downstream owner must confirm real product semantics before applying any private implementation change.
Merge, release, deployment, and production authority remain outside this packet.
